Operating system

DeveloperVarious
Written inC, C++, assembly
Kernel typeMonolithic, microkernel, hybrid

An operating system (OS) is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources, and provides common services for computer programs. Time-sharing operating systems schedule tasks for efficient use of the system, and may also include accounting software for cost allocation of processor time, mass storage, peripherals, and other resources.

History

The first computers of the late 1940s and 1950s were directly programmed either with plugboards or with machine code. The introduction of operating systems emerged with the shift toward storing programs in memory.

The term operating system covers many roles that are historical accidents of how systems evolved together over decades.

Types

Single-tasking and multi-tasking

A single-tasking system can only run one program at a time, while a multi-tasking operating system allows more than one program to run in concurrency.

Single- and multi-user

Single-user operating systems have no facilities to distinguish users, but may allow multiple programs to run in tandem.

Examples

  1. Linux — an open-source kernel licensed under GPL.
  2. Microsoft Windows — a proprietary family of OSes from Microsoft.
  3. macOS — Apple's desktop operating system based on Darwin.
